content.comment_body: Hello, hope you're doing well. I'm struggling to open a project that was created in [product_name] [version_no] using [product_name] [version_no] software. I’m being asked for a password, but it's not one we've set, as we can still access it with [product_name] [version_no]. Is there a default password set by [company_name] to prevent opening the program?
Could you share a screenshot of the password prompt?

[product_name] [version_no] recognizes the program as password protected. It requests the password during opening in [product_name] [version_no], while [product_name] [version_no] does not. This seems to be a new feature introduced by [company_name].
I created a simple program for a [article_no] and set the password to "Test." You can try opening it with both [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] [version_no] to observe the difference.

It opens automatically in [product_name] [version_no], but in [product_name] [version_no] you have to enter a password. Is there a way to use [product_name] [version_no] to communicate with the latest [product_name] series ([version_no], firmware [version_no])?
No. Any interaction between [product_name] and [product_name] devices, such as uploading or downloading programs, or online testing, requires [product_name] [version_no].

Alternatively, you could try opening the project with [product_name] [version_no], selecting everything in the diagram, and copying it. Then, paste into a new blank diagram. Keep in mind, all references will be lost in the process and will need to be manually recreated.
If you wish, feel free to send the project via private message and I can take a look.
I suspect the password for my project was numeric. Am I correct that [product_name] [version_no] now requires a password containing only letters?
Yes, [product_name] [version_no] only accepts passwords made up of letters.

If my existing password is numeric, I guess it's not possible to open the project in [product_name] [version_no]? I’m coping and pasting for now, but would appreciate knowing if there are alternatives for future transfers.
Do you know the password? Do you also have access to an older [product_name] version? If so, you could use the older software to remove the password (if you know it).

analysis.insight_summary: Users have encountered confusion because [product_name] [version_no] asks for a project password when opening files created with older versions, whereas previous releases did not request passwords. This is due to newly introduced features in [product_name] [version_no], resulting in unexpected hurdles for users migrating projects. Unclear guidance around compatibility and data transfer has also contributed to frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate smooth transitions and interoperability between [product_name] software versions, without encountering unexpected password prompts or loss of functionality.
